claim: More time and information yield better decisions is widely accepted.
source_text: It is widely accepted that more time and information yield better decisions.
evidence_reasoning: This statement refers to established scientific consensus about decision-making processes.

claim: Some decisions manage to be extremely fast and yet accurate.
source_text: However, some decisions manage to be extremely fast and yet accurate.
evidence_reasoning: This refers to established knowledge about a class of rapid decisions documented in the literature.

claim: Highspeed decisions use simplifying heuristics that work well for the most common condition but lack flexibility otherwise.
source_text: The trick of such highspeed decisions appears to be the use of simplifying heuristics that works well for the most common condition but lacks flexibility otherwise.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established understanding in the field about how highspeed decisions operate, based on prior research and theoretical frameworks.

claim: Archerfish observe the initial speed, direction, and height of falling prey and use these initial values to turn right towards where ballistically falling prey would later land.
source_text: In this decision, archerfish observe the initial speed, direction, and height of falling prey and then use these initial values to turn right towards where ballistically falling prey would later land.
evidence_reasoning: This describes previously established behavior of archerfish documented in prior research.

claim: Adult archerfish could reprogram their highspeed decision to a new non-ballistic rule.
source_text: We discovered that, surprisingly, adult fish could reprogram their highspeed decision to the new rule.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript (Figure 4).

claim: After reprogramming, fish were immediately able to generalize their decision to novel untrained settings.
source_text: Moreover, after reprogramming their decision fish were immediately able to generalize their decision to novel untrained settings, showing a remarkable degree of abstraction in how the decision circuit represented the novel rule.
evidence_reasoning: This finding is supported by experimental data from generalization tests (Figure 5).

claim: The decision circuit is capable of simultaneously using two distinct sets of rules, one for each of two visually distinct objects.
source_text: The decision circuit is even capable of simultaneously using two distinct sets of rules, one for each of two visually distinct objects.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data showing fish responding differently to triangles versus disks (Figure 6).

claim: The archerfish decision is made in less than 100 ms.
source_text: The flexibility and level of cognition are unexpected for a decision that lacks a speed-accuracy tradeoff and is made in less than 100 ms.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by latency measurements in the current study and cited previous research.

claim: The expected trade-off between the speed of a decision and its accuracy is very well documented across many species from slime mold to primates.
source_text: The expected trade-off between the speed of a decision and its accuracy is very well documented not only in humans but for many decisions across many species from slime mold to primates (Chittka et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Chittka et al., 2009.

claim: A class of very rapid decisions appears to deviate from the speed-accuracy tradeoff rule.
source_text: A class of very rapid decisions appears, however, to deviate from this rule (e.g. VanRullen and Thorpe, 2001; Romo and Salinas, 2001; Uchida et al., 2006; Stanford et al., 2010; Stanford and Salinas, 2021; Gladwell, 2005; Gigerenzer, 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Rats can reliably categorize odors based on just one sniff (about 300 ms), and more sampling time leads to no further improvement.
source_text: For example, rats can reliably categorize odors based on just one sniff (about 300 ms), and more sampling time leads to no further improvement.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Uchida et al., 2006 and related studies.

claim: In archerfish turn decisions, no relation was found between the average response latency and the accuracy of the turns.
source_text: In this decision, no relation was found between the average response latency and the accuracy of the turns (Schlegel and Schuster, 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Schlegel and Schuster, 2008.

claim: Humans can reliably classify natural visual images after surprisingly brief glimpses of only 20–40 ms.
source_text: Humans can reliably classify natural visual images after surprisingly brief glimpses (of only 20–40 ms, see VanRullen and Thorpe, 2001; Bacon-Macé et al., 2005; Uka and DeAngelis, 2003; Harwerth et al., 2003; De Bruyn and Orban, 1988; Snowden and Braddick, 1991; Nachmias, 1967; Tulunay-Keesey and Jones, 1976)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Hitters in baseball have only 400 ms to move their bat to the optimal strike point, a movement that can only be based on about 70 ms of visual processing.
source_text: For example, hitters in baseball have only 400 ms to move their bat to the optimal strike point, a movement that can only be based on about 70 ms of visual processing (Higuchi et al., 2016; Gray and Cañal-Bruland, 2018; Kidokoro et al., 2019).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to studies on baseball hitting.

claim: Decisions that lack a speed-accuracy trade-off manage to be so fast because they profit from using simplifying heuristics.
source_text: One reason could be that the decisions that lack a speed-accuracy trade-off manage to be so fast because they profit from using simplifying heuristics (Gladwell, 2005; Gigerenzer, 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This is an explanatory hypothesis supported by citations and logical inference.

claim: Male hoverflies use a rapid open-loop strategy to catch passing females based on hardwired assumptions about speed, size, and acceleration.
source_text: An elegant series of experiments showed that this very rapid and accurate decision is based on hardwired assumptions about the speed v and size (and hence detection distance D) of a typical female hoverfly and about the typical maximum rate a of the male's acceleration. These variables appear all to be genetically imprinted in the neural circuits that govern the male turn decision.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on cited work by Collett and Land, 1978.

claim: Challenging male hoverflies with objects that deviated from their hardwired assumptions caused them to make robust errors predicted by a simple heuristic model.
source_text: Expectedly, challenging the males with objects that deviated from these assumptions, caused them to make robust errors that were predicted based on a simple heuristic model that the fly appears to use (Collett and Land, 1978).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Collett and Land, 1978.

claim: Archerfish down aerial prey with shots of water and use an open-loop strategy to arrive simultaneously with their prey as soon as it hits the water surface.
source_text: Archerfish down aerial prey with shots of water and also use an open-loop strategy to arrive simultaneously with their prey as soon as it hits the water surface.
evidence_reasoning: This describes established archerfish behavior documented in prior research.

claim: Depending on visual contrast, water temperature, height of prey, and the distance from the future landing point, fully accurate turns can be initiated in as little as 40 ms.
source_text: Depending on visual contrast, water temperature, height of prey, and the distance from the future landing point, fully accurate turns can be initiated in as little as 40 ms (Schlegel and Schuster, 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Schlegel and Schuster, 2008.

claim: Archerfish can respond appropriately from a large range of distances and initial orientation and when encountering targets of unusual size or speed.
source_text: In contrast to the conditions in the male hoverfly, the ecological constraints in archerfish do not allow similar simplifying assumptions and archerfish can respond appropriately from a large range of distances and initial orientation and when encountering targets of unusual size or speed (as will be shown below).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and inference from ecological constraints.

claim: Archerfish predictive C-start decisions are among the fastest C-starts known in fish and are initiated much faster than an Olympic sprinter can respond to the start gun.
source_text: Their so-called predictive C-start decisions are among the fastest C-starts known in fish and are initiated much faster than an Olympic sprinter can respond to the start gun (Sillar et al., 2016; see Video 1 for an appreciation of the decision's speed).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation and reference to video data in the manuscript.

claim: When archerfish faced prey that was prevented from falling and only slid on top of a glass plate, their response latency was the same as in tests with real falling prey.
source_text: When many such interspersed rare cases with sliding flies were later analyzed, it turned out that fish still responded, although nothing fell. Moreover, their response latency – measured between the onset of prey motion and the onset of the turns – was the same as in most tests in which real prey was falling (Rossel et al., 2002).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Rossel et al., 2002.

claim: For each set of conditions with sliding flies, the fish had turned to the appropriate virtual impact point calculated based on ballistics.
source_text: This analysis revealed that for each set of conditions the fish had turned to the appropriate virtual impact point, calculated based on ballistics, just as they would toward a real later impact point of real falling prey (Rossel et al., 2002).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Rossel et al., 2002.

claim: The archerfish's turn decisions exclusively use information that is sampled during a brief interval after onset of prey motion.
source_text: The archerfish's turn decisions exclusively use information that is sampled during a brief interval after onset of prey motion (Schlegel and Schuster, 2008; Reinel and Schuster, 2014; Reinel and Schuster, 2018a; Reinel and Schuster, 2018b).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The information used in archerfish turn decisions includes the initial height from which prey is falling.
source_text: This information even includes the initial height from which prey is falling (Reinel and Schuster, 2018a).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Reinel and Schuster, 2018a.

claim: All experiments available have shown that the start decision does not use or has no access to prior information.
source_text: In other words, all experiments available have shown that the start decision does not use or has no access to prior information. Instead, it relies exclusively on information sampled once prey starts moving.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from multiple cited experiments.

claim: All archerfish studied so far in the lab and in the wild consistently showed robust turn decisions towards the inferred ballistic landing points.
source_text: Because all archerfish studied so far in the lab and in the wild consistently showed robust turn decisions towards the inferred ballistic landing points (Schlegel and Schuster, 2008; Rossel et al., 2002; Rischawy et al., 2015; Reinel and Schuster, 2014; Reinel and Schuster, 2018a; Reinel and Schuster, 2018b; Wöhl and Schuster, 2006; Wöhl and Schuster, 2007)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The authors expected the archerfish decision to be hardwired to ballistics.
source_text: we expected the decision to be hardwired to ballistics.
evidence_reasoning: This represents the authors' initial hypothesis before conducting the experiments.

claim: Hardwiring the decision circuit to ballistic falling patterns could be fixed genetically and/or established during the early ontogeny of the fish.
source_text: Hardwiring the decision circuit to ballistic falling patterns could be fixed genetically and/or established during the early ontogeny of the fish.
evidence_reasoning: This represents a hypothetical mechanism for how hardwiring could occur.

claim: The VR system presents the information with sufficient spatial and temporal resolution as needed by the decision circuit.
source_text: First, it must present the information with sufficient spatial and temporal resolution as needed by the decision circuit.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by the experimental results showing equivalent performance with VR and real stimuli (Figure 3).

claim: There is no statistically detectable difference between virtual and real responses in the VR system.
source_text: Third, the VR system would have to work so well that there is no statistically detectable difference between virtual and real responses.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical comparisons presented in Figure 3C-G.

claim: The setup worked with an LCD screen at a frame rate of 120 frames per second.
source_text: The setup worked, surprisingly, with an LCD screen at a frame rate of 120 frames per second and employed custom-made automatic feeders that were non-transparent and provided food at the right time and place, coupled to the motion shown on the screen.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the actual experimental setup used in the study.

claim: Operating the feeders without showing motion on the screen failed to elicit turn decisions.
source_text: Operating the feeders without showing motion on the screen failed to elicit turn decisions.
evidence_reasoning: This is an experimental result demonstrating that feeders alone do not trigger responses.

claim: When feeders were placed systematically offset from ballistic virtual impact points, turns were aimed at the VIPs and not at the feeders.
source_text: Most importantly, when feeders were placed not at the ballistic virtual impact points (VIPs) but systematically offset from them, then turns were aimed at the VIPs and not at the feeders – even though this was where the fish got their reward (Figure 3B; 15° offset, n=353; 30° offset, n=198).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data with specific sample sizes.

claim: The decisions made to ballistic VIPs were equivalent to those made with real falling objects in all examined aspects (accuracy, latency, kinematics).
source_text: Given the limitations in the temporal resolution of the screen it is striking that no aspect of the decisions was statistically different under real and virtual conditions (Figure 3C–G, n=101 (real) and n=85 (virtual) starts).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical comparisons of multiple parameters between real and virtual conditions.

claim: The accuracy of the aim achieved at the end of the turns was not statistically different between real and virtual conditions (p=0.506).
source_text: The accuracy of the aim achieved at the end of the turns (measured as introduced in Figure 2) was not statistically different (p=0.506, Mann-Whitney; Figure 3C)
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific statistical result from the comparison of real and virtual conditions.

claim: The turns had the same latency between real and virtual conditions (p=0.297).
source_text: The turns also had the same latency (between onset of prey motion and onset of the turns; p=0.297; Mann-Whitney; Figure 3D)
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific statistical result from the comparison of real and virtual conditions.

claim: The new rule generates a systematic and substantial deviation of 14.9 cm between the new VIPs and the ballistic VIPs.
source_text: It generates a systematic and substantial deviation (of 14.9 cm) between the new VIPs and the ballistic VIPs as inferred from the initial movement.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a calculated parameter of the experimental design.

claim: After the new rule, the movement direction is deflected by 39.8° to the left.
source_text: After having traveled straight throughout what was the previous decision time, the movement direction is deflected by 39.8° (to the left, s. Methods)
evidence_reasoning: This describes a specific parameter of the experimental manipulation.

claim: Response probability remained constant across all training blocks during training with the new deflected trajectories (p>0.08).
source_text: Interestingly, the fish never ceased to respond with their characteristic turns (response probability remained constant across all training blocks, p>0.08, Pairwise Chi-square).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from analysis of training data.

claim: The kinematics of the turns and latency remained constant during training with deflected trajectories (bending and straightening phase both p>0.28, latency p>0.07).
source_text: The kinematics of the turns and latency also remained constant (bending and straightening phase of their C-starts both p>0.28, latency p>0.07; Kruskal-Wallis).
evidence_reasoning: These are statistical results from analysis of training data.

claim: After more than 1750 presentations (55 experimental days), the turns clearly minimized the error to the appropriate new 'deflected' VIPs and no longer to the ballistic ones.
source_text: However, gradually the errors made to the new 'deflected' VIPs became smaller and, after more than 1750 presentations (55 experimental days), the turns clearly minimized the error to the appropriate new 'deflected' VIPs (Figure 4C, E, F; Video 4) and no longer to the ballistic ones.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data over an extended training period.

claim: The errors made in interspersed tests showing only the initial linear part were not different from those made when the full trajectories were visible.
source_text: The errors made in the interspersed tests (n=68) were not different from those made when the full trajectories were visible (Figure 4G).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical comparison of errors under different test conditions.

claim: In tests with initial movement offset from feeder position, turns were still aimed at the new deflected VIPs and not at the feeders or ballistic VIPs.
source_text: Yet, the turns the fish made in these tests were still aimed at the new deflected VIPs (differences from zero error p=0.721 at 15° (n=197) and p=0.113 at 72° (n=145); One-Sample t-tests) but not at the feeders and also not at the ballistic VIPs (Kruskal-Wallis: p≤0.001 at 15°; p=0.005 at 72°; Dunn's p<0.05 for comparison of errors; Video 5).
evidence_reasoning: These are statistical results from critical control experiments.

claim: The new turns were possible and equally accurate across a range of distances and turn angles.
source_text: Finally, the new turns were not restricted to just a few positions and orientations of the responding fish. Rather, they were possible and equally accurate across a range of distances and turn angles (Figure 4H, I).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by data showing performance across different spatial conditions.

claim: There was no significant linear or Spearman correlation between error magnitude and response latency in the re-programmed decisions.
source_text: For both plots, there was no significant linear (p=0.318, R2=0.005, Figure 4J; p=0.469, R2=0.004, Figure 4K) or Spearman correlation (p=0.128 and 0.174, respectively, in Figure 4J, K).
evidence_reasoning: These are statistical results demonstrating absence of speed-accuracy tradeoff.

claim: A highspeed decision that lacks a speed-accuracy tradeoff can be flexibly reprogrammed to a new rule.
source_text: Our findings, therefore, demonstrate that a highspeed decision that lacks a speed-accuracy tradeoff can be flexibly reprogrammed to a new rule.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: All training to the new rule was carried out exclusively with targets presented at only one height level.
source_text: This can be examined conveniently because all training to the new rule was carried out exclusively with targets presented at only one height level.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a specific constraint of the experimental design.

claim: The turns already minimized the error to the VIPs appropriate for untrained novel height levels right from start with no trend that errors would decrease.
source_text: Interestingly, the turns already minimized the error to the VIPs that were appropriate for the untrained novel height levels. They were appropriate right from start with no trend that errors would decrease (linear regression: all p>0.1).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis of performance at novel heights.

claim: At untrained height levels, turns minimized the error to the deflected landing point (both p>0.07) and were not directed to the ballistic landing point (both p<0.001) or the substitute prediction (both p<0.001).
source_text: A detailed analysis of the errors (Figure 5D, E) showed that the turns minimized the error to the deflected landing point also at the untrained height levels (difference from zero: both p>0.07; One-Sample t-test). They were also not directed to the ballistic landing point (prediction 'ballistic;' both p<0.001; One-Sample Signed Rank) and not towards the deflected landing point at the training height (prediction 'substitute;' both p<0.001; One-Sample Signed Rank).
evidence_reasoning: These are statistical results from generalization tests at novel heights.

claim: The new rule is not represented by updating a simple lookup table but in a way that allows immediate generalization to new untrained height levels.
source_text: In other words, the new rule is not represented by updating a simple lookup table but in a way that allows immediate generalization to the new untrained height levels.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion inferred from the generalization test results.

claim: When faced with untrained prey sizes, the trained fish immediately turned to the deflected landing points (p>0.4 for difference from zero error).
source_text: Again, the trained fish immediately turned to the deflected landing points (differences from zero error: each p>0.4, One-Sample Signed Rank; difference in aim before and after size change p=0.764, Mann-Whitney)
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from generalization tests with novel prey sizes.

claim: Learning did not involve simplifying a priori assumptions about absolute prey size.
source_text: Hence, learning did also not involve simplifying a priori assumptions about absolute prey size.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the successful generalization to novel prey sizes.

claim: At untrained speed levels, the first 30 turns minimized the error to the actual deflected VIP (p=0.102) but not to the ballistic VIP (p<0.001) or substitute prediction (p<0.001).
source_text: When tests with lower than training speed were interspersed among presentations with the speed levels as during training, then already the first 30 turns made at the lower speed (Figure 5G) minimized the error to the actual deflected VIP (difference from zero p=0.102; One-Sample t-test), but not to the VIPs given by either ballistics (prediction 'ballistic;' p<0.001; One-Sample Signed Rank) or by using predictions for the deflected VIPs that are based on the trained speed levels (p<0.001; One-Sample Signed Rank).
evidence_reasoning: These are statistical results from generalization tests at novel speeds.

claim: All tests show that the decisions had been reprogrammed in much more clever ways than predicted, allowing immediate generalization.
source_text: In summary, all tests show that the decisions had been reprogrammed in much more clever ways than predicted. Rather than independently changing the size of an unrewarding turn for each individual constellation – as would seem required because the input variables themselves are varied independently from each other – learning allowed immediate generalization.
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary conclusion drawn from all generalization test results.

claim: When shown ballistic objects after training on deflected trajectories, turns made in response to the ballistic object initially still minimized the error to the deflected VIP (p=0.256) and not to the ballistic VIP (p=0.038).
source_text: However, in experiments to test this prediction, the turns made in response to the 'ballistic object' (rewarded at the ballistic VIP) initially still minimized the error to the deflected VIP (difference from zero error p=0.256; One-Sample Signed Rank; same variance as for disk p=0.343; Brown-Forsythe; first 160 responses to ballistic object) and not to the ballistic VIP point (difference to ballistic landing point: p=0.038, Mann-Whitney; Figure 6B, C).
evidence_reasoning: These are statistical results from experiments testing dual rule usage.

claim: After about 300 additional encounters of moving triangles, the turns minimized the error to the ballistic impact point when a triangle was shown (p=0.836 for ballistic, p=0.020 for deflected).
source_text: After about 300 additional encounters of moving triangles the turns minimized the error to the ballistic impact point when a triangle was shown (error to ballistic VIPs p=0.836, error to deflected VIPs p=0.020; One-Sample Signed Rank; Figure 6B).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result showing learning of the second rule.

claim: The turns continued to minimize the error to the deflected impact point whenever the disk was shown (error to ballistic p≤0.001, error to deflected p=0.084).
source_text: However, the turns continued to minimize the error to the deflected impact point whenever the disk was shown (error to ballistic p≤0.001, error to deflected p=0.084, n=187; One-Sample Signed Rank; Figure 6C).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result showing maintenance of the first rule while learning the second.

claim: In tests showing only initial straight paths, turns were toward the ballistic landing point when the triangle was shown and to the deflected landing point when the disk was shown.
source_text: Again, the turns were toward the ballistic landing point when the triangle was shown (difference from ballistic p=0.075, from deflected p<0.001; One-Sample Signed Rank) and to the deflected landing point when the disk was shown (difference from ballistic p=0.008, from deflected p=0.412; One-Sample Signed Rank) (Figure 6D).
evidence_reasoning: These are statistical results from critical tests of dual rule usage.

claim: Latency (p=0.189) and kinematics (p=0.984) of the turns were the same in the responses to triangles and disks.
source_text: Also, latency (p=0.189, Mann-Whitney; Figure 6E) and kinematics of the turns (bending duration; p=0.984; Mann-Whitney; Figure 6F) were the same in the responses to triangles and disks.
evidence_reasoning: These are statistical results comparing turn characteristics for different objects.

claim: Object shape determined which rule the decision used to determine the appropriate turn given the input data.
source_text: In other words, the nature of the turn decision was the same, but object shape determined which rule the decision used to determine the appropriate turn given the input data.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion inferred from the experimental results with different shapes.

claim: All three individual fish that contributed most starts minimized the error to the appropriate VIP (all p>0.1 for difference from zero error).
source_text: Our analysis showed that all three of the three individual fish that had contributed most of the starts in Figure 6 minimized the error to the appropriate VIP (Figure 6G; difference from zero error always p>0.1; One-Sample Signed Rank).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from individual fish analysis.

claim: The variability of the errors in applying the two rules did not differ in any of the individuals (p=0.966).
source_text: Also, the variability of the errors in applying the two rules did also not differ in any of the individuals (p=0.966; Brown-Forsythe).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from individual fish analysis.

claim: The decision circuit used by archerfish has the potential of simultaneously operating on two different rules.
source_text: This shows clearly that the decision circuit used by archerfish does have the potential of simultaneously operating on two different rules.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the individual fish analysis results.

claim: When shape was revealed only at motion onset, the decisions remained appropriate to the ballistic (p=0.451) or deflected (p=0.671) VIPs.
source_text: Under these conditions, the decisions remained appropriate to the ballistic (triangle; n=109 starts) or deflected (disk; n=46 starts) VIPs (difference from zero error to appropriate VIP: p=0.451 (triangle) and p=0.671 (disk); p≤0.001 for the alternatives, all One-Sample Signed Rank).
evidence_reasoning: These are statistical results from tests without prior shape information.

claim: The distribution of errors was not statistically different when shape cue was available 2 s prior versus only during decision phase (p=0.269).
source_text: Furthermore, also the distribution of errors was not statistically different from those obtained with the shape cue available 2 s prior to the decision (p=0.269; Brown-Forsythe).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical comparison of error distributions under different timing conditions.

claim: The information needed to select which rule is to be used can be extracted in the very brief interval after motion onset, together with all other decision-relevant information.
source_text: Hence the information that is needed to select which rule is to be used can also be extracted in the very brief interval after motion onset, together with all other decision-relevant information.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the results showing successful rule selection without prior information.

claim: Highspeed decisions that demonstrably lack a speed-accuracy tradeoff do not necessarily lack flexibility.
source_text: Using the rapid turn decisions of hunting archerfish as an example we demonstrate that highspeed decisions that demonstrably lack a speed-accuracy tradeoff (Figure 4J, K, Schlegel and Schuster, 2008), do not necessarily lack flexibility.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the experimental findings.

claim: The decision is not hardwired to ballistic falling patterns.
source_text: Before, the fish would turn to the later ballistic landing point, based on the initial values of prey motion. After a training phase in which the connection between initial motion and the point of reward had been systematically changed – according to a new rule – the fish were able to rapidly turn towards the new points, that were appropriate for their starting position and the combination of initial motion variables.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is directly supported by the training and testing results.

claim: None of the cognitive aspects described in archerfish highspeed decisions is unique and not found in much slower behaviors.
source_text: None of the cognitive aspects we describe here is in any way unique and not found in much slower behaviors.
evidence_reasoning: This statement draws on established knowledge about cognitive abilities across different behaviors.

claim: Archerfish generalize efficiently when they learn how to engage moving targets and to judge the absolute size of prey.
source_text: For example, archerfish generalize efficiently when they learn how to engage moving targets and to judge the absolute size of prey (Schuster et al., 2004; Schuster et al., 2006).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Recognizing and assigning a value to different visual shapes has been demonstrated in archerfish.
source_text: Also, recognizing and assigning a value to different visual shapes has been demonstrated much earlier (e.g. Rischawy and Schuster, 2013)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Many cognitive aspects have been described across the animal kingdom, including animals with far smaller brains.
source_text: and many aspects have been described across the animal kingdom, including animals with far smaller brains (Chittka and Niven, 2009; Chittka and Jensen, 2011; Giurfa, 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: What is surprising is to find cognitive features in a decision made at reflex-like speed (less than 100 ms) that lacks a speed-accuracy tradeoff.
source_text: What is surprising, therefore, is clearly not to find cognitive features in archerfish, but rather to find such features in a decision that is made at a very different timescale at reflex-like speed (less than 100 ms) and that lacks a speed-accuracy tradeoff (Figure 4J, K; Schlegel and Schuster, 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretive statement based on the experimental findings and their context.

claim: The complexity involved in reprogramming the archerfish highspeed decision is comparable to tasks considered highly sophisticated in laboratory animals.
source_text: The complexity involved in reprogramming the archerfish highspeed decision must also not shy a comparison with tasks that are considered highly sophisticated in many laboratory animals (e.g., Asaad et al., 1998; Bunge, 2004; Fusi et al., 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative inference supported by citations to sophisticated tasks in other species.

claim: The task the decision circuit of archerfish can handle in as little as 40 milliseconds is to conditionally switch between two complete rules of how to connect a three-dimensional set of input data to a continuum of possible motor outputs.
source_text: In comparison, the task the decision circuit of archerfish can handle in as little as just 40 milliseconds (see Figure 4) is not only to conditionally switch between two motor outputs but to switch between two complete rules of how to connect a three-dimensional set of input data to a continuum of possible motor outputs.
evidence_reasoning: This characterization is based on the experimental findings and analysis of task complexity.

claim: Substantial progress has been made showing that smaller brains do not necessarily have reduced cognitive capacities.
source_text: Substantial progress has been made on this latter assertion, resulting in an impressive and continuously growing list of sophisticated cognitive features that were found in animals with bird- and fish brains (Bshary et al., 2002; Shettleworth, 2010; Güntürkün and Bugnyar, 2016).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to research on cognition in animals with smaller brains.

claim: Insect brains that operate with a millionth of the neurons of a human brain can handle a wide range of cognitive tasks.
source_text: Most impressively, it has been demonstrated that insect brains that operate with a millionth of the neurons of a human brain can handle a wide range of cognitive tasks (Chittka and Niven, 2009; Chittka and Jensen, 2011; Giurfa, 2013; Giurfa et al., 2001; Avarguès-Weber et al., 2012; Chittka, 2017)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to research on insect cognition.

claim: Insect cognitive tasks include social or observational learning.
source_text: that even include social or observational learning (Chittka, 2017; Loukola et al., 2017; Bridges et al., 2023).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to research on social learning in insects.

claim: Learning can lead to the reprogramming of innate and supposedly hardwired behaviors in insects.
source_text: Of particular interest in our context is that it has even been demonstrated that learning can lead to the reprogramming of innate and supposedly hardwired behaviors in insects (Roussel et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Roussel et al., 2012.

claim: The kinematics of archerfish turn decisions is completely equivalent to the C-starts that the fish produce to escape.
source_text: In the turn decisions of archerfish, specifically, it is known that the kinematics of their turn decisions is completely equivalent to the so-called C-starts that the fish produce to escape (Wöhl and Schuster, 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Wöhl and Schuster, 2007.

claim: Both the turn decisions and the archerfish escape C-starts are among the fastest C-starts known in fish.
source_text: Both the turn decisions (also called predictive C-starts; Schuster, 2023) and the archerfish escape C-starts are among the fastest C-start known in fish (Wöhl and Schuster, 2007)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The motor circuits for archerfish turns are restricted to hindbrain circuits organized around the giant Mauthner neuron.
source_text: and so at least the motor circuits are restricted to the well-known powerful hindbrain circuits of a comparably small number of tractable numbers of neurons, organized around the giant Mauthner neuron (Korn and Faber, 2005; Machnik et al., 2018a; Machnik et al., 2018b; Hecker et al., 2020).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to research on C-start neural circuits.

claim: The Mauthner neuron's rapidly conducting axon would be suited to initiate the turn but recruitment of other hindbrain neurons is needed to account for the precision and adjusted straightening speed.
source_text: Its rapidly conducting axon would be suited to initiate the turn but the recruitment of other hindbrain neurons is needed to account for the precision and adjusted straightening speed of the fish (Wöhl and Schuster, 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about neural mechanisms supported by citation.

claim: Rapid and precise turn decisions are required because of the severe competition archerfish face from other surface-feeding fish.
source_text: First, rapid and precise turn decisions are required because of the severe competition archerfish often face. Other surface-feeding fish are not only more numerous in Thailand – and, therefore, likely to be closer at the landing point of the archerfish's prey – but they are better equipped with mechanosensors and are also capable of using vision to guide pre-impact turns. It is, therefore, crucial for archerfish to outperform them by using fast and precise turn decisions (Rischawy et al., 2015).
evidence_reasoning: This is an ecological explanation supported by citation to Rischawy et al., 2015.

claim: The clearly demonstrated capacity of these decisions for being flexible has evolved because of competition and scarcity of aerial prey.
source_text: We suggest that the clearly demonstrated capacity of these decisions for being flexible has evolved because of this competition and because of the scarcity of aerial prey at least in many natural habitats.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative evolutionary explanation proposed by the authors.

claim: Small prey will typically fall ballistically while larger prey will face considerable frictional forces and will not fall equally far.
source_text: This requires the fish to down and efficiently secure prey of various sizes. While small prey will typically fall ballistically (Rossel et al., 2002; Reinel and Schuster, 2018a), larger prey will face considerable frictional forces and – all other conditions being equal – will, therefore, not fall equally far.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on physics and supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Simply using hardwired circuitry for ballistically falling prey would produce wrong initial turns for larger items and would require subsequent corrections that cost precious time.
source_text: Simply using hardwired circuitry for ballistically falling prey would produce wrong initial turns for these larger items and would require subsequent corrections that cost precious time and might mean losing some of the advantage over the competitors.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the consequences of hardwired circuitry.

claim: The flexibility found and the ability to operate on at least two types of prey would allow individual archerfish to efficiently handle two types of prey that co-occur during a specific time of the year.
source_text: The flexibility we found and the ability to operate on at least two types of prey that fall according to two different rules would allow at least some individual archerfish to efficiently handle two types of prey that co-occur during a specific time of the year.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference about ecological advantages of the observed flexibility.

claim: The ecological constraints and severe competition that archerfish face in the wild could have favored the evolution of a decision that has the potential for plasticity and for combining speed, accuracy, and flexibility.
source_text: So, we suggest, clearly without proof, that the ecological constraints and the severe competition that archerfish face in the wild could have favored the evolution of a decision that has the potential for plasticity and for combining speed, accuracy, and flexibility.
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly stated as a speculative suggestion without proof.

claim: Highspeed decisions that lack a speed-accuracy tradeoff can offer learning capacities and cognitive aspects of much slower decisions and behaviors that occur at least at 100 times lesser speed.
source_text: Our findings demonstrate that highspeed decisions that lack a speed-accuracy tradeoff are not necessarily limited to operating based on simplifying heuristics but can, at least in principle, offer learning capacities and cognitive aspects of much slower decisions and behaviors that occur at least at 100 times lesser speed.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the experimental findings.

claim: It will be exciting to see if the capacities found in archerfish are special or perhaps much more widespread among other highspeed decisions.
source_text: First, it will be exciting to see if the capacities we found in archerfish are special or perhaps much more widespread among other highspeed decisions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.

claim: The findings suggest that rapid decision-making can be efficiently used in many technological applications in which time is premium – even if such applications require a high degree of flexibility.
source_text: Third, the findings suggest that rapid decision-making can be efficiently used in many technological applications in which time is premium – even if such applications require a high degree of flexibility.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference about potential technological applications.

claim: Experiments were conducted on a group of six adult archerfish (Toxotes chatareus).
source_text: Experiments were conducted on a group of six adult archerfish (Toxotes chatareus).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental subjects used in the study.

claim: All objects used in this study had a Michelson contrast of 0.96.
source_text: All objects used in this study had a Michelson contrast of 0.96, as determined with a luminance meter (LS-110 Konica Minolta Sensing Europe) under the conditions of the actual experiments.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a measured parameter of the experimental stimuli.

claim: Objects that mimicked ballistically falling motion moved at a horizontal speed of 1.775 m/s and their virtual landing occurred 243 ms later, after a virtual path of 43 cm.
source_text: Objects that mimicked ballistically falling motion moved at a horizontal speed vh = 1.775 m s–1 and their virtual landing occurred 243 ms later, after a (virtual) path of 43 cm.
evidence_reasoning: This describes specific parameters of the experimental stimuli.

claim: All recordings were made from below through the tank's transparent bottom.
source_text: All recordings were made from below through the tank's transparent bottom (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: All experiments on the start decisions require the competition within a group.
source_text: Because all experiments on the start decisions require the competition within a group (Schlegel and Schuster, 2008)
